mainTopic: Arranging a גט through messengers, רבי יוסי's ruling on passing spoken instructions to an agent, and the praise of the חכמים
overview: The amud opens with a worry about a husband who sends messengers to arrange a גט. The fear is that, so as not to shame the סופר, they will let him sign as a witness even though the husband never said so. The גמרא first answers that such cases are rare, because arranging a גט this way is 'כשר ולא תעשה'. It then finds that this answer fails for the opinion that the practice is allowed from the start. So it gives a new answer: רבי יוסי made two separate rulings, and שמואל agrees with only one of them. Next the גמרא examines רבי's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, that spoken instructions cannot be passed on to an agent. רבי defends it by saying 'נמוקו עמו', his reasoning is always with him, and איסי בן יהודה's list praising the great חכמים backs this up. Finally the גמרא explains why a גט arranged through messengers should be avoided even though it is valid: a woman might hire people to give false instructions. It ends with a dispute among several pairs of אמוראים over a husband who tells two people to have a סופר write the גט and to sign it themselves.

steps.title: The worry about embarrassing the scribe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes describing a worry: the husband says 'tell a סופר to write and so-and-so to sign,' and the messengers, not wanting to shame the סופר, let him sign with one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Let us worry that the husband said:] 'Tell a scribe to write, and tell so-and-so and so-and-so to sign.' Then, so the scribe won't feel shamed, they have one of those witnesses sign together with the scribe, but the husband never said to do that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a worry it started raising. The worry is that the messengers might change who signs the גט, against the husband's instructions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband named two specific עדים. The סופר might feel insulted that he was not trusted to sign, so the messengers swap him in for one witness. Since the husband did not authorize this, the גט would be invalid, and people might mistakenly think it is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Scribe, the one who writes the גט

phrases.english: "Tell a scribe and he will write,
and tell so-and-so and so-and-so and they will sign";
and because of the shame of the scribe, they are concerned
phrases.notes: The סופר might feel hurt, as if he were not trusted enough to sign as a witness.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַחְתְּמִי חַד מֵהָנָךְ סָהֲדִי, וְסוֹפֵר בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: and they have one of those witnesses sign, with the scribe together with him,
but the husband did not say to do so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a worry that began before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a גט arranged through messengers can be trusted to follow the husband's instructions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The messengers may let the סופר sign to spare his feelings, which the husband never authorized, so the גט would be invalid.

steps.title: Such a case is uncommon
steps.stepSummary: Since this way of arranging a גט is 'valid, but should not be done in ישראל,' it rarely happens, so we do not worry about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Master said that such a גט is 'valid, but this should not be done in Israel,' it is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry. A husband sending messengers this way is unusual, so חכמים do not make a rule to guard against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If done, a גט arranged through messengers is כשר, but people are taught not to do it this way at the start. Because of that, the case is לא שכיח, and חכמים do not make a גזירה for uncommon situations.

keyTerms.meaning: But it should not be done this way in ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: 'כשר ולא תעשה' does not mean the גט is invalid. It is valid after the fact, just not the proper way to do it at the start.

phrases.english: Since the Master said:
"It is valid, but this should not be done in Israel,"
phrases.notes: The husband himself should appoint the סופר and the עדים, not send messengers to do it.

phrases.english: it is not common.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rarity: חכמים do not make a גזירה for uncommon cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We should worry that the messengers will let the סופר sign
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is לא שכיח, so there is no worry

steps.title: The same worry when the husband tells two people to sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe the husband told two people 'tell a סופר to write and you sign,' and they let the סופר sign with one of them instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let us worry that the husband said to two people: 'Tell a scribe to write, and you sign.' Then they, because of the scribe's shame, go and have the scribe sign together with one of them, but the husband never said to do that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new version of the same worry. This time the husband names the two messengers themselves as the עדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case seems like it could be more common than the first one. Again the messengers might swap in the סופר for one of themselves, which the husband did not authorize, and that would make the גט invalid.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵיחוּשׁ דִּילְמָא אֲמַר לְהוּ לְבֵי תְרֵי:
phrases.english: And let us be concerned that perhaps he said to two people:
"Tell a scribe and he will write, and you sign,"
and these two go, because of the shame of the scribe,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַחְתְּמִי לֵיהּ לְסוֹפֵר בַּהֲדֵי חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: and have the scribe sign together with one of them,
but the husband did not say to do so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵיחוּשׁ דִּילְמָא אֲמַר לְהוּ לְבֵי תְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a parallel case to test the answer of step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the worry is לא שכיח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here the husband speaks directly to the two people who will sign, so maybe this case is common enough to worry about.

steps.title: This case is also 'valid but should not be done'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: this case too is 'כשר ולא תעשה,' so it is also uncommon.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: This too is a case of 'valid, but should not be done.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before. This setup is also not the proper way to arrange a גט, so it is rare and we do not worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning from step 2 is applied to the new case. Because this practice is also discouraged from the start, it is לא שכיח, and no גזירה is needed.

phrases.english: They say: This too
is a case of "valid, but should not be done."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָא נָמֵי כָּשֵׁר וְלֹא תֵּעָשֶׂה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 using the reasoning of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the same rarity reasoning to a parallel case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two-people case might be common enough to worry about
steps.terutzMaskana: It is also 'כשר ולא תעשה,' so it is rare

steps.title: What about the view that this may be done from the start?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for the view that this case is 'כשר ולא תעשה,' but what about the view that it is 'כשר ותעשה,' allowed from the start?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who said 'valid, but should not be done.' But according to the one who said 'valid, and it may be done,' what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. It points out that there is another opinion that allows this practice from the start, and then the 'rare case' answer does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 4 depends on the practice being discouraged. According to the opinion that it is 'כשר ותעשה,' people would do it often, so the worry about the סופר comes back. The גמרא is now looking for a different answer for that opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
Valid, and it may be done from the start

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who said: "Valid, but should not be done";
but according to the one who said: "Valid, and it may be done,"
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4 by pointing to a different opinion
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the two-people case is 'כשר ולא תעשה' and therefore rare
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the opinion that it is 'כשר ותעשה,' the practice is allowed and common, so the rarity answer fails and the worry returns.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the earlier answer depends on one side of a מחלוקת, so the גמרא must find another answer that works for both views.

steps.title: רבי יוסי made two separate rulings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the difficulty: רבי יוסי said two separate things. שמואל agrees with one and disagrees with the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוסי said two things, and שמואל agrees with him on one and disagrees with him on the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its earlier attempts and gives a new answer. רבי יוסי actually made two separate rulings, so שמואל can follow one and not the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, it looked like שמואל contradicted himself by following רבי יוסי and also allowing 'tell a סופר to write.' Now we see these are two different rulings of רבי יוסי. The first is that spoken instructions cannot be handed on to an agent. The second is that even 'tell someone to write' cannot be handed on. שמואל accepts the first ruling and rejects the second.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier approach is dropped and a new one is coming
He said two things, meaning two separate rulings
He holds like him, meaning he agrees with him

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל agrees with רבי יוסי that spoken instructions (מילי) cannot be passed on to an agent. He disagrees about a husband who explicitly said 'tell a סופר to write': in that case the job can be passed on.
steps.whyThisMatters: Splitting רבי יוסי's view into two rulings removes the apparent contradiction in שמואל's statements without any need for the worry about shaming the סופר.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yosei said two things;
phrases.notes: The two things: spoken instructions can't be handed to an agent, and even 'tell someone to write' can't be handed on.

phrases.english: and Shmuel agrees with him in one,
and disagrees with him in one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by dropping the 'rarely happens' approach altogether.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the authority's view is split into two independent rulings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought שמואל's agreement with רבי יוסי had to rest on the worry about shaming the סופר, which ran into trouble with the view that the case is 'כשר ותעשה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי made two rulings. שמואל follows the one that מילי cannot be passed to an agent and rejects the one about 'tell a סופר'.

steps.title: רבי rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to שמואל's statement in the name of רבי: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי that verbal instructions cannot be passed to an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the statement itself: שמואל said in the name of רבי that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, who said that spoken instructions cannot be passed on to an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ruling it quoted earlier and studies it on its own. This sets up the next question about why רבי ruled this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ruling was only used as background for a contradiction. Now it becomes the main topic, and the next step will question it.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. It is used to return to a statement quoted earlier and examine it directly
Cannot be handed over to an agent

phrases.english: The matter itself: Shmuel said that Rebbi said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to this statement, quoted earlier in passing, to look at it on its own.

phrases.english: The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei,
who said spoken instructions cannot be handed over to an agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from resolving the contradiction to examining the ruling itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: spoken instructions (מילי) cannot be passed on to an agent.

steps.title: Why follow one opinion against two?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון ברבי asks his father why he ruled like רבי יוסי when רבי מאיר and חנינא איש אונו both disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון the son of רבי said to him: since רבי מאיר and חנינא איש אונו argue with רבי יוסי, what made you rule like רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי's son challenges the ruling. Two חכמים hold the opposite view, so why follow the one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is about how a ruling is decided. With two against one, you would normally expect the הלכה to follow the larger side. So רבי needs a special reason to side with רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: He said before him, a respectful way of speaking to a greater person
What did he see, meaning what was his reason

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rebbi, said before him:

phrases.aramaic: מֵאַחַר שֶׁרַבִּי מֵאִיר וַחֲנִינָא אִישׁ אוֹנוֹ
phrases.english: Since Rabbi Meir and Chanina of Ono
disagree with Rabbi Yosei,
what did Rebbi see to say
the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵאַחַר שֶׁרַבִּי מֵאִיר וַחֲנִינָא אִישׁ אוֹנוֹ חוֹלְקִין עַל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מָה רָאָה רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling stated in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two תנאים (רבי מאיר and חנינא איש אונו) oppose a single one, so the ruling seems to go against the majority.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's reasoning is always with him
steps.stepSummary: רבי tells his son to be quiet. Had he seen רבי יוסי, he would know that רבי יוסי's rulings always come with solid reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: be quiet, my son, be quiet. You never saw רבי יוסי. Had you seen him, you would know his reasoning is always with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers that רבי יוסי was special. His rulings always rest on solid reasons, so it is right to follow him even against two others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not about this one case. It is about the kind of scholar רבי יוסי was. Because his opinions were always well grounded, he is followed even against more voices.

keyTerms.meaning: If only, or had it been that
His reasoning is with him: his rulings always come with solid reasons

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the general rule that the הלכה often follows רבי יוסי in his arguments, because 'נמוקו עמו'.

phrases.english: He said to him: Be quiet, my son, be quiet,
you did not see Rabbi Yosei;
had you seen him, you would know his reasoning is with him.
phrases.notes: Meaning: every ruling he gave came with solid reasons behind it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתוֹק בְּנִי שְׁתוֹק לֹא רָאִיתָ אֶת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Justifying the authority: the quality of reasoning outweighs the number of opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The majority (רבי מאיר and חנינא איש אונו) should decide.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי is followed because his rulings are always well reasoned (נמוקו עמו).

steps.title: איסי בן יהודה's list of the חכמים' praises
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי's description: איסי בן יהודה listed the special quality of each חכם, and he described רבי יוסי as 'נמוקו עמו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: איסי בן יהודה used to list the praises of the חכמים. רבי מאיר is a scholar and a scribe. רבי יהודה is a scholar when he wants to be. רבי טרפון is a pile of nuts. רבי ישמעאל is a well-stocked store. רבי עקיבא is a full storehouse. רבי יוחנן בן נורי is a peddler's basket. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is a basket of spices. The teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is small in amount but clean. רבי יוסי's reasoning is with him. רבי שמעון grinds a lot and brings out a little.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that רבי's praise of רבי יוסי was well known. In איסי בן יהודה's list, רבי יוסי is described with the very words 'נמוקו עמו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a short picture of each great חכם's style of learning. For the argument here, the key line is about רבי יוסי. It confirms that the חכמים knew him for well-grounded reasoning, which backs רבי's choice to rule like him.

keyTerms.meaning: Small in amount but clean (a קב is a small measure)
Grinds a lot and brings out a little

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ruled like רבי יוסי against two others because of the well-known quality 'נמוקו עמו': his rulings always rest on solid reasoning. The ברייתא of איסי בן יהודה confirms this.
steps.confusionAlert: This list is praise for every חכם, not criticism. Even lines like 'a scholar when he wants to be' or 'grinds a lot and brings out a little' appear in a list the ברייתא calls their praises.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Isi ben Yehuda
would list the praises of the Sages:
Rabbi Meir: a scholar and a scribe;
Rabbi Yehuda: a scholar when he wants to be;
Rabbi Tarfon: a pile of nuts;
Rabbi Yishmael: a well-stocked store;
Rabbi Akiva: a full storehouse;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי – קוּפַּת הָרוֹכְלִים;
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri: a peddlers' basket;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה – קוּפָּה שֶׁל בְּשָׂמִים;
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya: a basket of spices;

phrases.aramaic: מִשְׁנַת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב – קַב וְנָקִי;
phrases.english: the teaching of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov: small in amount but clean;
phrases.notes: Literally 'a קב and clean.' A קב is a small measure, so: not much, but pure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei: his reasoning is with him;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן – טוֹחֵן הַרְבֵּה וּמוֹצִיא קִימְעָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon: grinds a lot and brings out a little.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה הָיָה מוֹנֶה שִׁבְחָן שֶׁל חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי's statement 'נמוקו עמו' in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's claim that רבי יוסי's rulings are always well reasoned
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of איסי בן יהודה, which describes רבי יוסי as 'נמוקו עמו'

steps.title: Explaining the description of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains איסי בן יהודה's description of רבי שמעון: he forgot only a little, and what he forgot was only chaff.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון forgets only a little, and whatever he lets go of is only bran, the unimportant part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a short ברייתא that explains the praise of רבי שמעון in איסי בן יהודה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture is a miller sifting flour. The good flour stays and only the bran falls away. In the same way, רבי שמעון kept the important teachings, and anything he forgot was of little value.

keyTerms.meaning: Bran, the waste part of the grain

phrases.english: It was taught: he forgets a little,
phrases.notes: This explains how איסי בן יהודה described רבי שמעון in the list from the previous step.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַה שֶּׁמּוֹצִיא – אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא אֶלָּא סוּבִּין.
phrases.english: and what he removes, he removes only bran.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains one entry in איסי בן יהודה's list of the חכמים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון forgot very little, and only the unimportant parts.

steps.title: רבי שמעון tells his students his rulings are the best
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון tells his students to learn his rulings, because they are the choicest of רבי עקיבא's rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so רבי שמעון said to his students: My sons, learn my rulings, because my rulings are the best of the best of רבי עקיבא's rulings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the praise of רבי שמעון with his own words to his students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the 'bran' picture, this shows that רבי שמעון kept only the finest part of what he learned. He says his rulings are the cream taken from the cream of his teacher רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The choicest of the choicest, the best part taken from the best part

phrases.english: And likewise רבי שמעון said to his students:
My sons, learn my rulings,
for my rulings are the choicest of the choicest
of the rulings of רבי עקיבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanation in step 11 with רבי שמעון's own words
steps.raayaObject: The description of רבי שמעון as keeping only the finest teachings
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's statement to his students

steps.title: Back to the case: telling two people to have a גט written and signed
steps.stepSummary: Returning to an earlier case, רב הונא in the name of רב rules that such a גט is כשר, but this should not be done in ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the case itself. A husband told two people: 'Tell a סופר to write the גט, and tell so-and-so and so-and-so to sign it.' רב הונא said in the name of רב: the גט is כשר, but this should not be done in ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses 'גופא' to go back and look closely at a ruling it mentioned earlier. רב says the גט works after the fact, but this way of doing things should be avoided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the husband does not speak directly to the סופר and the witnesses. He passes his instructions through two messengers. רב says the גט is still valid, but one should not do it this way to begin with. The next steps ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a statement it quoted earlier
This should not be done in ישראל, meaning avoid it from the start

steps.confusionAlert: 'כשר' and 'לא תעשה זאת' do not contradict each other. The גט works after the fact, but you should not set things up this way to begin with.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
If he said to two people:
'Tell a scribe and he will write,
and tell so-and-so and so-and-so and they will sign' —

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rav: it is valid,
but this shall not be done in Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the praise of the חכמים and returns to examine רב's ruling quoted earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט written and signed through instructions passed by two messengers is כשר after the fact, but this should not be done to begin with.

steps.title: If it is valid, why avoid it?
steps.stepSummary: עולא asks רב נחמן (or the reverse): if the גט is כשר, why should it not be done?
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to רב נחמן, and some say רב נחמן said to עולא: Since it is valid, why should this not be done in ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא challenges רב's ruling and asks for the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question points out a tension. If the method produces a valid גט, there seems to be nothing wrong with it. So what is the reason to avoid it?

phrases.english: Ulla said to Rav Nachman,
and some say Rav Nachman said to Ulla:
Since it is valid,
why shall this not be done in Israel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵאַחַר דְּכָשֵׁר, אַמַּאי לֹא תֵּעָשֶׂה זֹאת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second half of רב's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the גט is valid, there seems to be no reason to avoid this method.

steps.title: The worry: she might hire witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The answer: we worry that a woman might hire witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We are worried that the woman might hire witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The other אמורא answers with the reason: there is a risk that a woman could hire people to set up a fake גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people get used to a גט being arranged through messengers, a woman could hire two people to falsely say the husband sent them. The סופר and the signers would then never hear it from the husband himself. That is why the method is avoided even though it is valid.

phrases.english: He said to him:
We are concerned lest she hire witnesses.
phrases.notes: 'She' is the wife. She might hire people to falsely say the husband sent them.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason behind the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A valid method should have no reason to be avoided
steps.terutzMaskana: It is avoided because of the worry that a woman might hire people to arrange a fake גט

steps.title: But we do not worry about forged witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the worry from a ברייתא: the חכמים did not worry about forgery by witnesses signed on a sale document or on a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we really worry about this? Isn't it taught in a ברייתא: for witnesses signed on a field sale document or on a woman's גט, the חכמים were not worried about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer by citing a ברייתא that seems to say we do not suspect witnesses of this kind of fraud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says we do not suspect signed witnesses of forging a sale document or a גט without the owner or husband agreeing. That seems to contradict the worry that a woman would hire witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Document for the sale of a field

phrases.english: But are we concerned?!
But isn't it taught:
Witnesses who are signed on a field of sale,
and on a woman's bill of divorce —
the Sages were not concerned about this matter!
phrases.notes: 'This matter' means the worry that the document was made without the owner or husband agreeing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 15
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the חכמים do not suspect signed witnesses of forging a גט, so why worry about hired witnesses?

steps.title: They won't forge it themselves, but they might tell someone else to
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses would not commit the forgery themselves, but they might casually tell someone else to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would not do the act themselves, but they would say words and tell someone else to do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating doing a forgery from merely speaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is right that witnesses would not sign a forged גט themselves. But people take speaking more lightly than acting. Hired messengers might tell a סופר and signers to act, and those people would not know anything is wrong. So the worry about using messengers still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not do an act

steps.whatToRemember: A גט arranged through messengers who instruct the סופר and witnesses is כשר, but it is avoided. People who would never forge a גט themselves might still give a false spoken instruction to others.

phrases.english: An act they do not do,
but speech they do say.
phrases.notes: He means they won't forge the גט themselves, but might tell a סופר and signers to make one, and those people won't know anything is wrong.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 and keeps the worry of step 15 in place
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between doing an act and saying words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If witnesses are not suspected of forgery, there is no reason to worry about hired witnesses
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses are not suspected of forging with their own hands, but they may give a false spoken instruction to others

steps.title: Husband tells witnesses to instruct the scribe: רב חסדא vs. רבה בר בר חנה
steps.stepSummary: A husband tells two people to have a scribe write the גט and to sign it themselves. רב חסדא says it is כשר but should not be done this way. רבה בר בר חנה says it is כשר and may be done this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man said to two people, 'Tell the scribe to write the גט, and you two sign it': רב חסדא says it is valid, but it should not be done this way. רבה בר בר חנה says it is valid, and it may be done this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new case: the husband passes his instruction to the scribe through the witnesses, instead of telling the scribe himself. Two אמוראים give different rulings on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the גט works once it has been made, so no one says it is פסול. They argue only about doing it this way from the start. רב חסדא says avoid it, and רבה בר בר חנה says it is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Scribe: the person who writes the גט.
'Sign!': the husband tells the two witnesses to sign the גט.
Valid, but it should not be done this way from the start.
Valid, and it may be done this way even from the start.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'ולא תעשה' as saying the גט is invalid. Everyone here holds the גט is כשר. The argument is only about whether to do it this way in the first place.

phrases.english: If he said to two people: 'Tell the scribe and he will write,'
phrases.notes: 'He' is the husband, and the two people are going to be the witnesses.

phrases.english: 'and you sign' –
Rav Chisda says: 'It is valid, but it should not be done,'

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר: ״כָּשֵׁר וְתֵעָשֶׂה״;
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana says: 'It is valid, and it may be done.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִשְׁנַיִם: ״אִמְרוּ לְסוֹפֵר וְיִכְתּוֹב, וְאַתֶּם חֲתוֹמוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of why something כשר should still not be done, the גמרא brings a new case with the same 'כשר ולא תעשה' question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the husband tells the witnesses to have the scribe write the גט and to sign it themselves, the גט is כשר. רב חסדא says this should not be done from the start. רבה בר בר חנה says it may be done.

steps.title: Two more pairs of אמוראים split the same way
steps.stepSummary: The same argument repeats in two more pairs: רב נחמן vs. רב ששת, and רבה vs. רב יוסף. In each pair, one says 'don't do it' and the other says 'it may be done.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says it is valid but should not be done; רב ששת says it is valid and may be done. רבה says it is valid but should not be done; רב יוסף says it is valid and may be done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists two more pairs of אמוראים who argue about the same case in the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added about the case itself. What we learn is that this was a wide argument across several generations of אמוראים, not just two people. In every pair, everyone agrees the גט is כשר; they differ only on doing it this way from the start.
steps.whatToRemember: In this case, everyone agrees the גט is כשר. Three pairs of אמוראים argue only about doing it this way from the start: רב חסדא, רב נחמן and רבה say 'don't do it'; רבה בר בר חנה, רב ששת and רב יוסף say 'it may be done.'
steps.confusionAlert: רבה here is not the same person as רבה בר בר חנה in the previous step. The names look alike, but they are two different אמוראים.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman says: 'It is valid, but it should not be done,'
Rav Sheshet says: 'It is valid, and it may be done.'
Rabba says: 'It is valid, but it should not be done,'
Rav Yosef says: 'It is valid, and it may be done.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: ״כָּשֵׁר וְלֹא תֵּעָשֶׂה״, רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: ״כָּשֵׁר וְתֵעָשֶׂה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It adds more pairs of אמוראים who argue about the same case in the same way as in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן and רבה hold that it is כשר but should not be done. רב ששת and רב יוסף hold that it is כשר and may be done.
